solves: Shows how much of a long process is done, such as an upload or a sign-up in steps, or that it is under way while there is still no value.
use_when: When the process takes more than a few seconds and the system knows how much is done, or into how many fixed steps it splits.
determinate whenever there is a percentage.
indeterminate only until the first real value arrives, and switch to determinate as soon as it does.
steps when the process has a few fixed, known steps, such as a sign-up: show the N of M and say the current step in the help text.
At the end, show success or error with the icon and the help text, because the bar must not stay stopped at a partial value.
md in the body of the screen and sm in dense places, such as the header of a flow or a card.
Show the value as text next to the bar, because the track is subtle and the text gives the exact value.
do_not_use_when: For a short wait with no value: use nph-spinner.
As a fixed level meter, such as used space or a grade: progress changes over time; for a fixed level, show only the value as text.
Without a label or an aria-label: the screen reader does not know what it measures.
As navigation between the steps of a flow: the steps type only shows progress; to mark each step, use nph-stepper.
As an adjustment control: the person does not drag or choose the value; use nph-slider.

type.constraint: It is the Figma property tipo. determinate draws the proportion of value; indeterminate draws a segment one third of the track that runs in a loop, while there is no value; steps splits the bar into equal segments, one per fixed step. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the parts by it. Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

size.constraint: It is the Figma property tamanho. md is the 8 px bar for the body of the screen; sm is the 4 px bar for dense places. Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

status.constraint: It is the Figma property status. On determinate, success and error exist only at value 100; on steps, with any number of steps; indeterminate has only active. Success and error bring the status icon and, on error, the help text is required. Reflects because the colors come from it. Any other value, or a status that does not exist on the type, draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

value.constraint: From 0 to 100, read on determinate. In the Figma set the values are the samples 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100; on screen the value is continuous. At 0 the indicator disappears and only the end stop remains. A value that is not a number from 0 to 100 draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

steps.constraint: The number of steps, read on steps: 3, 4 or 5, the counts of the accepted Figma set. Required on steps; any other count draws nothing and emits console.error in development. Another count is a pending decision of Indiane (D-1 of DSA-65).

step.constraint: The current step, an integer from 1 to steps, read on steps. On active, the steps up to the current one are done and the rest pending; on error, the current step is the one with the error. Outside 1 to steps, the bar draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

label.constraint: The visible label above the bar, already localized. It names the bar for the screen reader. Empty turns the part off, and then the aria-label of the host is the name.

value-text.constraint: The text next to the label, already localized: the percentage ("50%"), the "N of M" on steps, or a state word on indeterminate and on error ("In progress", "Error on step 3"). It is also the aria-valuetext. Empty turns the part off.

help.constraint: The help text below the bar, already localized. It describes the bar for the screen reader. On error it is required and says what failed and what to do; without it the bar draws and warns in development.

aria-label.constraint: The accessible name when label is not given. The label wins over it. A bar with neither draws and warns once in development.

type.choose_when: determinate when there is a percentage; indeterminate while there is no value yet; steps when the process has 3, 4 or 5 fixed steps.
do_not_combine_with: status success or error on indeterminate

size.choose_when: md in the body of the screen; sm in dense places, such as the header of a flow or a card.

status.choose_when: active while the process runs; success and error when it ends, with the icon and the help text.
do_not_combine_with: success or error on determinate below 100

active.changes_for_user: The indicator, or the done segments, show how much is done.

success.changes_for_user: The bar and the icon circle-check take the success color, and the help text tells it ended.

error.changes_for_user: The bar, the icon circle-xmark and the help text take the error color, and the help text says what failed.

indeterminate-loop.changes_for_user: A segment one third of the track runs from the left edge to the right edge, in one pass of 1400 ms, linear, in a loop.

business_rules: The bar is not interactive: it has no hover, pressed or focus state and no focus ring. An action such as Cancel is an nph-button next to it.
The track is decorative: alone it carries no information. The value shows as text and the end shows through the end stop.

Below 100 the end stop, 4 x 4 on both sizes and never taller than the bar, shows at the end of the track, and progress/track-gap separates the indicator from the rest of the track, so the indicator is slightly shorter than the exact proportion. The exact value is the text one.
The width is fluid, 100% of the container, with a minimum of 48 px. There is no width token.
The loop exists only while there is no value: when the first real value arrives, the consumer switches to determinate. With reduced motion, the loop stops and the segment rests at the start.
The color comes from the status: there is no free color.
On steps, the current step has the color of the done ones: the N of M and the help text say which step the person is on.
Success and error show the status icon, and on error the help text is required: color alone does not explain.
domain_errors: Success or error on determinate below 100, or on indeterminate: the bar draws nothing and emits console.error in development.
Error without help: the bar draws and warns in development.

tokens.label: progress/label-foreground
tokens.segment: progress/segment-background, progress/segment-background-pending, progress/segment-background-success, progress/segment-background-error, progress/segment-gap, progress/segment-radius

ai_hints: Use nph-progress for a long process the system can measure or split into fixed steps; for a short wait with no value, use nph-spinner.
Use determinate whenever there is a percentage, and indeterminate only until the first real value arrives; then switch the type.
Always give a label, or an aria-label when the label is off, because the label is the accessible name.
At the end, set success or error with value 100 and the help text; on error, the help text says what failed.
On steps, give steps (3, 4 or 5) and the current step, and write the N of M in value-text and the current step in help.
Do not use nph-progress as navigation between steps or as a fixed level meter.

accessibility.semantics: The track is a progressbar with aria-valuemin 0 and aria-valuemax 100. Determinate gives aria-valuenow the value; steps gives it the share of steps, counting the current one, with the N of M in aria-valuetext; indeterminate omits it. The status icon is decorative.
accessibility.accessible_name: The label, by aria-labelledby; with no label, the aria-label of the host. The help text is the description.
accessibility.focus: The bar does not receive focus and has no focus ring.
accessibility.contrast: Label, value text and help text, including the error one, pass 4.5:1 over the background in both themes. The indicator and the done, success and error segments pass 3:1 against the background and against the track, in both themes. The track and the pending segment are decorative.
accessibility.color_alternative: Success and error also show through the status icon and the help text. The value shows as text. On steps, the N of M and the help text say which step the person is on.

invalid_combinations: Success or error on determinate below 100 — the contract has them only at value 100.
Success or error on indeterminate — it has only active.
Steps with a count other than 3, 4 or 5, or a step outside 1 to steps.
A free color, a width token or a focus state — the color comes from the status and the bar is not interactive.
An error without the help text — color alone does not say what failed.
anti_patterns: Using the bar for a short wait with no value.
Using the bar as a fixed level meter.
Leaving the bar without a label or an aria-label.
Using the steps bar as navigation between steps.
Leaving the bar stopped at a partial value at the end of the process.
